newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nizhny Novgorod delays Eurobond to July.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nizhny Novgorod delays Eurobond to July.

text.p: Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region will issue its debut Eurobond in July, not in June as the region planned before, a regional administration finance official said on Tuesday.
"By our firm estimates and those of the federal government the issue will be in July," the region's Finance Department Deputy Head Alexander Pogodin told Reuters.
He said the region, of which First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov was governor, had not yet managed to register the issue prospectus with the Finance Ministry, which had slowed the progress.
Nizhny Novgorod plans to issue a five-year paper, led by ING-Barings, for up to $100 million.

Nizhny Novgorod is one of three Russian regions and municipalities allowed by a presidential decree to issue a Eurobond. The two others, the City of Moscow and St Petersburg, have already tapped international markets.
